newsitem.title: USA: Oklahoma bomb defense attacks witnesses.
newsitem.headline: Oklahoma bomb defense attacks witnesses.

text.p: Attorneys for Oklahoma City bombing defendant Timothy McVeigh launched an attack Wednesday on the reliability of witnesses whose testimony prosecutors plan to use to obtain a conviction.
The attorneys, in a written filing, want the trial judge to suppress the testimony of seven witnesses, arguing that the government's procedures were tainted.
"None of the potential witnesses the government will call at trial can make a positive identification of Mr. McVeigh," his lawyers said.
The identification is tainted, in part, because some of the witnesses saw news photos of McVeigh before being asked by authorities to identify him, McVeigh's lawyers alleged.

According to the filing only one of the prosecution's witnesses claims to possibly have seen McVeigh and a Ryder rental truck in front of the Alfred P. Murrah Federal Building just before a truck bomb exploded in 1995.
McVeigh and former Army buddy Terry Nichols are accused of the bombing. McVeigh is to go on trial March 31 and Nichols at an undetermined later date. Both face the death penalty if convicted.
A prosecution spokeswoman said the government's formal written response to Wednesday's challenge is due in two weeks.
